BREAKING: Bitcoin falls nearly -$2,000 in 20 minutes as $400 million worth of levered longs are liquidated in under one hour. https://t.co/hVnLfd156z

"That's how delusional these Bitcoiners are. He found something that was counter to all his work, and he decided to turn the findings upside down to fit his narrative"

This hilariously off base.

This finding was not "counter"  to my work... it's at the literal CORE of my work.

Bitcoin is unflinching.

It just keeps spitting out block after block every ~10 minutes.

But the human psychology around this thing is constantly shifting and evolving.

The crowd often gets too bullish and too bearish at the wrong times. So it's incredibly useful to see where people are at emotionally. It can give us a more holistic understanding of the Bitcoin market.

Understanding this better can help us weather volatility. Bitcoin can be damn hard to HODL when price is down and it seems like no one wants Bitcoin anymore.

But here's the thing.

This is exactly the most bullish time to buy.

I could obviously be wrong, we could have some news break and Bitcoin tanks.

This is always on the table.

But buying Bitcoin (a narrative/psychologically driven asset) when moods are historically low seems like a layup IMO.

Time will tell which of us is right.

Y'all know which side I'm on.

The employment downturn in the US Information sector is intensifying:

Information employment fell another -10,000 jobs in September, to 2.739 million, the lowest since December 2020.

Excluding the 2020 pandemic drop, this is the lowest level since December 2014.

In total, the Information industry has shed -376,000 jobs, or -12.1%, since the November 2022 peak.

To put this into perspective, during the 2001 recession and its aftermath, Information employment fell -568,000 jobs, or -15.3%, from March 2001 to December 2003.

The Information sector is losing jobs at a crisis pace.

BREAKING: The total volume of payments processed on crypto cards has reached a record $12.5 billion, up +140% year-to-date.

This also marks +247% growth compared to levels seen in October 2025.

Continued adoption of stablecoins as a payment rail and the push toward cross-border transaction efficiency are behind the surge in volume.

Furthermore, QR-code based payments for crypto cards are seeing robust growth.

This has fueled +55% quarter-over-quarter growth in activated cards on Jupiter Spend, one of the largest onchain card providers, particularly due to demand for QR payments.

Crypto cards are the next phase of crypto adoption.

I’m going to be brutally honest here.

A part of me didn’t want to publish any of this.

I’ve been asked repeatedly to use some of this sentiment data to trade, and I’ve often urged people not to. I’m a long-term HODLer myself, and I've seen how painful it can be to try to time your Bitcoin buys.

But I find myself in an interesting position.

Because some of the sentiment data I’ve been sitting on has been extremely high-signal. Historically, buying during low readings has produced stronger returns than buying during high readings.

That’s a big claim.

So it deserves scrutiny.

But the longer I’ve spent with this data, the more confident I've become that I’m sitting on something valuable. So today I’m going to share the strongest (though slightly counterintuitive) signal I’ve found so far.

Not greed.

Not fear.

Desire.

How badly the crowd WANTS Bitcoin to pay off.

I’ve tracked tons of different emotions in Bitcoiners’ language, using data spanning most of the past decade. I've learned a lot and seen many positive correlations, but this one stood out above all others.

I’ve talked about desire before.

But today, I want to show you what Bitcoin’s returns looked like after the highest and lowest readings historically, and why that matters for Bitcoin today.

Looking at the heat map below, we see that trailing EPS are up 30% from a year ago, with the n12m estimate expected to grow another 20%. The margin story continues to impress with another new high clocking in at 17.4 last week. Who wants to step in front of a train like that? Yet, the price that investors are willing to pay for these blockbuster earnings and margins is going down. Investors don’t want to pay top dollar for possibly peak earnings growth, especially as the US Government offers you a risk-free rate of 5.3% nominal and 2.9% real. Plus, that pesky Fed Model is work.
 
That’s some stiff competition. That rising risk free rate is having its impact on anyone or anything with a vulnerable balance sheet. That includes companies down the quality spectrum, most consumers, and of course, Governments near and far. Just look at French Government bonds as exhibit A (middle of heatmap). 

These opposing forces are holding the equity indices in a vice, with only 25% of the market above its 50-day MA and 46% above their 200-day MA. A stealth correction. If the rate pressures subside, it’s easy to see the indices accelerate higher again, especially with the weak seasonals soon ending. But for now, ignore the Fed Model at your peril.

The US high-yield credit market stress is rising:

Credit spreads for CCC-rated and lower corporate bonds are up to 12.0%, their widest level since November 2022.

Over the last 5 months, this figure has surged +298 basis points, surpassing the April 2025 peak of 11.4%.

This represents a comparable increase to that seen during the 2022 bear market and the February-April 2025 market correction.

If this pace continues, credit spreads for the lowest-rated US corporate bonds will exceed the 2022 peak of 12.9% as soon as this month.

To put this into perspective, the 2020 pandemic high was 19.6%.

Credit stress is rising sharply beneath the surface.
